name: French Polynesia
rule: DBS’s current private-import guidance, updated 5 August 2026 and citing Order 324 CM, expressly covers postal parcels. It waives both import permits and phytosanitary certificates for plant food that has undergone cooking, whether commercially/industrially prepared or otherwise. Camellia is absent from its listed prohibited cooked species. Applying that provision to the stated steam-manufactured sencha is an explicit processing inference. The authority’s reform notice confirms use of ISPM 32; the standard illustrates tea as Category 1. Full Annex 5 was not independently retrieved, so this finding rests on current DBS guidance, not the repealed 1996 order.
personalMailApplicability: The current DBS page expressly includes post. Declare the tea accurately, keep it commercially sealed and labelled, and allow arrival inspection. This assessment depends on actual steaming during manufacture; it does not cover merely dried raw leaves or herbal mixtures.

permitFreeReason: Current postal guidance supplies a published general cooked-plant-food exemption. Actual steam-manufactured pure sencha reasonably falls within it; that is a stated inference, supported by the authority’s current ISPM 32 framework. No special permit or foreign phytosanitary certificate is required under this published route. Ordinary declaration and arrival clearance remain.
paperworkType: Ordinary customs declaration and routine arrival inspection/clearance under the published cooked-food route.
requiredDocument: No special permit or phytosanitary certificate under the stated cooked-plant-food route; accurate declaration and original labelled packaging.
